trial_name.text: Study 1 / C/I98-316 (posaconazole vs fluconazole in HSCT recipients with GVHD)

citations.quote: C/I98-316 was a randomized double-blind active controlled trial of posaconazole versus fluconazole as control in HSCT recipients receiving high-dose immunosuppressive therapy for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).

nct.text: Not stated in the reviewed documents

citations.quote: C/I98-316 was a randomized double-blind active controlled trial of posaconazole versus fluconazole as control in HSCT recipients receiving high-dose immunosuppressive therapy for graft-versus-host disease (GVHD).

This was a Phase 3, randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active control, comparative study of Posaconazole (200 mg TID) versus Fluconazole (400 mg QD) in the prophylaxis of invasive fungal infections in high-risk subjects with GVHD following allogeneic hematopoietic progenitor cell (stem cell) transplantation.

design.text: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled: posaconazole oral suspension 200 mg three times a day vs fluconazole capsules 400 mg once daily

citations.quote: The first study (Study 1) was a randomized, double-blind trial that compared posaconazole oral suspension (200 mg three times a day) with fluconazole capsules (400 mg once daily) as prophylaxis against invasive fungal infections in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients with Graft versus Host Disease (GVHD).

population.text: Allogeneic HSCT recipients with Graft versus Host Disease (GVHD) receiving high-dose immunosuppressive therapy

citations.quote: The first study (Study 1) was a randomized, double-blind trial that compared posaconazole oral suspension (200 mg three times a day) with fluconazole capsules (400 mg once daily) as prophylaxis against invasive fungal infections in allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients with Graft versus Host Disease (GVHD).

endpoint.text: Composite endpoint of clinical failure (breakthrough proven/probable invasive fungal infection, mortality, and use of systemic antifungal therapy) through 16 weeks

citations.quote: clinical failure represented a composite endpoint of breakthrough IFI, mortality and use of systemic antifungal therapy.
*: Primary time point is at 16 weeks for study C/I98-316 and at end of oral therapy plus 7 days for study P01899.

As stated before, a total of 600 subjects were enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio (301 to posaconazole and 299 to fluconazole) at 90 sites of whom 21 did not receive study medication (10 in posaconazole arm and 11 in fluconazole arm).

result.text: Clinical success 202/301 (67%) posaconazole vs 189/299 (63%) fluconazole; 95.01% CI for the difference in success rates (-2.7, 12.2). All-cause mortality at 16 weeks similar: POS 58/301 (19%) vs FLU 59/299 (20%)

endpoint.text: Composite endpoint of clinical failure (breakthrough proven/probable invasive fungal infection, mortality, and use of systemic antifungal therapy) at end of oral therapy plus 7 days

citations.quote: clinical failure represented a composite endpoint of breakthrough IFI, mortality and use of systemic antifungal therapy.
*: Primary time point is at 16 weeks for study C/I98-316 and at end of oral therapy plus 7 days for study P01899.

As stated before, a total of 602 subjects were enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio (304 to posaconazole and 298 to fluconazole/itraconazole) at 110 sites of whom 13 did not receive study medication (7 in posaconazole arm and 6 in fluconazole/itraconazole arm).

result.text: Clinical success 166 (55%) posaconazole vs 126 (42%) fluconazole/itraconazole; 95.13% CI for the difference (4.3, 20.1). All-cause mortality at 100 days lower with posaconazole: POS 44/304 (14%) vs FLU/ITZ 64/298 (21%)

citations.quote: **: Difference, p-value and 95.13% confidence interval of the difference (POS – FLU/ITZ) using a normal approximation adjusted by the control-site and baseline stratification factor as described by Fleiss6.
all cause mortality was lower at 100 days for posaconazole-treated patients in Study 2 [POS 44/304 (14%) vs FLU/ITZ 64/298 (21%)].

indication.text: Prophylaxis of invasive Aspergillus and Candida infections in patients 13 years of age and older who are at high risk of developing these infections due to being severely immunocompromised, such as HSCT recipients with GVHD or those with hematologic malignancies with prolonged neutropenia from chemotherapy

citations.quote: NOXAFIL (posaconazole) is indicated for prophylaxis of invasive *Aspergillus* and *Candida* infections in patients, 13 years of age and older, who are at high risk of developing these infections due to being severely immunocompromised, such as hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients with Graft versus Host Disease (GVHD) or those with hematologic malignancies with prolonged neutropenia

target_moa.text: Triazole antifungal that blocks synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of the fungal cell membrane, by inhibiting the enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase

citations.quote: As a triazole antifungal agent, posaconazole blocks the synthesis of ergosterol, a key component of the fungal cell membrane, through the inhibition of the enzyme lanosterol 14\alpha-demethylase and accumulation of methylated sterol precursors.
Posaconazole is a new second generation triazole that blocks the synthesis of ergosterol by inhibiting lanosterol 14 alpha-demethylase.

key_safety.text: Most common treatment-emergent adverse events (at least 10% in the POS or FLU groups, pooled prophylaxis safety analysis) included fever (45%), diarrhea (42%), nausea (38%), vomiting (29%), headache (28%), abdominal pain (27%). Most serious concerns were hepatic toxicity (elevated LFTs, rare severe liver injury) and QTc prolongation.
